summary: At step 136, C’s Conflict-selected Purple Worm reaches its adjacent AT_ENGL/AD_DGST attack on the Stone Golem after the physical bite; JavaScript stops at mattackm()’s monster-engulf refusal. Port whole mhitm.c:gulpmm() and the consumed mdamagem()/uhitm.c:mhitm_ad_dgst() damage path, then wire mattackm()’s AT_ENGL arm. The lethal digestion reaches A83’s reserved mon.c monster-removal contract, which must be preserved when the attacker is restored to the swallowed monster’s square.

source.branch: With Conflict active, mon.c:movemon_singlemon() calls fightm() for a non-Wizard mover that can see the hero and its square within BOLT_LIM. The Purple Worm passes resist_conflict() and selects the adjacent Stone Golem. Its attacks are AT_BITE/AD_PHYS/2d8 followed by AT_ENGL/AD_DGST/1d10. The AT_ENGL arm applies the adjacent-distance guard, then requires the attack roll tmp > rnd(20+i), that the attacker is not already engulfing the hero, and that failed_grab() permits the target; the recorded rnd(21)=9 and subsequent swallow establish success. engulf_target() accepts the large Stone Golem because it is below MZ_HUGE, the Purple Worm is gigantic, neither is trapped, and both squares are legal. The M-to-M AD_DGST effect sets damage to the golem’s current hp; the Stone Golem is G_NOCORPSE, so it dies without leaving a corpse. gulpmm() then handles the returned defender-death status and keeps the living worm at the former defender square, as the step-137 screen shows.
callers: C: mon.c:movemon_singlemon() at 1306-1318 applies the Conflict gates and calls mhitm.c:fightm(). JS follows the same path through mon.js:movemon_singlemon() and its fightMonster operation.

C: mhitm.c:fightm() at 106-169 checks resistance, scans living monsters in list order, selects the first adjacent target, and calls mattackm(); it consumes the result flags. JS js/mhitm.js:fightm() at 396-445 is already implemented.

C: mhitm.c:mattackm() AT_ENGL at 510-535 applies the adjacent range, successful-hit, engulfing_u(), and failed_grab() checks before assigning gulpmm()’s result. JS js/mhitm.js:802-804 currently raises the observed UnsupportedTurnBoundaryError at this arm.

C: gulpmm() calls mdamagem() at mhitm.c:909-910 and consumes its status to select the defender-death, aggressor-death, or both-alive map-restoration arm at 913-964. mdamagem()’s return then contributes to mattackm()’s attack result and fightm()’s Conflict result.
dependencies: mhitm.c:engulf_target() returns the eligibility result consumed by gulpmm(). Its current JS implementation in js/mhitm.js:894-949 has both monster-side size, trap, and terrain checks and was written for this eventual gulpmm() caller; reuse it after verifying the live map-state inputs.

gulpmm() consumes mdamagem()’s status. mdamagem() calls uhitm.c:mhitm_adtyping() for its side effects, then calls uhitm.c:mhitm_knockback() and consumes its Boolean before applying mhm.damage. The knockback function is already implemented in JS; the C recording draws rn2(3) and rn2(6) on the swallow path.

uhitm.c:mhitm_adtyping() dispatches AD_DGST to the whole uhitm.c:mhitm_ad_dgst() helper at 4827. That helper sets mhm.damage to the defender’s current hp for M-to-M digestion, handles lifesaving and corpse/nutrition effects, and is still unported at js/uhitm.js:5403. gulpmm() sets gm.mswallower around mdamagem() because corpse_chance() reads that state; the Stone Golem’s G_NOCORPSE flag makes the no-corpse branch relevant.

After AD_DGST sets lethal damage, mhitm.c:mdamagem() calls mon.c:monkilled(); for this non-Rider Stone Golem, monkilled() reaches mondead() and the m_detach()/relmon() removal chain. mhitm.c:gulpmm() then consumes the DEF_DIED status and restores or relocates the Purple Worm. A83’s contract:mon-removal-conditional-completion and reservations on mon.c:mondead, m_detach, mon_leaving_level, and relmon are directly in this route; preserve that behavior. The route calls monkilled(), not xkilled().

gulpmm() also consumes goodpos(), minliquid(), and mintrap() results while recovering the attacker after a defender death; preserve their source order even though this recording leaves the worm at the golem’s former square without a liquid or trap transition.

nethack-c/upstream/src/uhitm.c:4492-4567 is the whole mhitm_ad_dgst() helper; :4782-4832 dispatches AD_DGST at 4827. The saved C path reaches it after gulpmm() installs gm.mswallower and calls mdamagem(); its lethal defender removal follows mhitm.c’s explicit comment at 918-926: mdamagem() -> monkilled() -> mondead() -> m_detach() -> relmon().

At examined commit 4901dd542af51235daa15e837437a78fa6af5787, js/mhitm.js:802-804 refuses M-to-M AT_ENGL; js/uhitm.js:5403 refuses mhitm_ad_dgst. The current js/mhitm.js:894-949 already implements the shared engulf_target() predicate, while mdamagem() at 1046-1130 is explicitly partial and its AD_DGST dispatch cannot proceed until the missing helper is wired.

The prior nonadjacent case investigations/synthetic/v21/wizard-conflict-purple-worm-m2m-dgst-stone-golem-v21-cfirst.json concern a different recording/hash and stop first at step 135 on hero-directed mhitu.c:mattacku() AT_ENGL -> gulpmu(). This assigned recording/hash stops at step 136 on monster-directed mhitm.c:mattackm() AT_ENGL -> gulpmm(), with C showing the monster swallow on step 137. The hero-directed gulpmu() finding does not explain this case.

Actual A83 reservations in .cache/A83-bear-trap-region-query-test-scope-event.json include contract:mon-removal-conditional-completion and source:mon.c:mondead, m_detach, mon_leaving_level, and relmon.
